title: LOEWE DYNAMIC TP 3.2 Pharmacological intervention in healthy participants using Esketamine and Midazolam to better understand dynamic networks
summary:
This study investigates how the brains of healthy participants respond to changes in the glutamate system. Esketamine, a medication that modulates glutamate signaling in the brain, is administered as a single dose. Additionally, two other groups are examined: a placebo group and a group receiving Midazolam (an active placebo). All substances are administered intranasally.

The effects of these substances are measured using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and electroencephalography (EEG) while participants perform tasks measuring working memory, reward anticipation, and language processing. To gain insights into participants' everyday well-being, questions and short voice recordings are collected regularly during the day via a smartphone app over a 9-day period (Ecological Momentary Assessment, EMA).

The aim of this study is to better understand how the brain functions, particularly how pharmacological substances influence dynamic brain networks, with the ultimate goal of developing new approaches to the research and treatment of psychiatric disorders
conditions: This study investigates healthy participants to explore the effects of pharmacological interventions on dynamic networks. The findings are intended to contribute to the development of new personalized treatment approaches for psychiatric disorders in the long term

interventions.name:
Esketamine
Esketamine is administered intranasally using a intranasal mucosal atmoization device (LMA-7300-MAD). It will be administered in five individual doses of 0.2 ml each, with an interval of 4 minutes between doses. The dose will depend on the weight of the participant (1mg/kg body weight).

Midazolam
Midazolam will be administered in the same manner as Esketamine.  The total dosage will be 5 mg.

Placebo 
A sterile saline solution is administered as a placebo in the same volume and via the same application route to ensure comparability of conditions

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- no contraindications for MRI 
- psychological and physiological health (as specified by the exclusion criteria)
Exclusion criteria:
- Psychiatric disorders (diagnosed using the MINI)
- Intolerance to the administered medications (Esketamine & Midazolam)
- Regular or acute medication use
- MRI-relevant metal implants or devices (e.g., pacemakers, prosthetics, intrauterine devices unless explicitly MRI-compatible, etc.) 
- Recent tattoos, tattoos with metallic ink, or permanent makeup
- Medical contraindications for Ketamine intervention (e.g., glaucoma, renal failure, liver dysfunction, hyperthyroidism, past or acute cardiomyopathy, hypertension)
- Medical contraindications for Midazolam intervention (e.g., chronic respiratory, renal, or heart failure, liver dysfunction, use of opioids or other benzodiazepines)
- Pregnancy
- History of ketamine abuse
- History or elevated risk of psychosis
- Insufficient German language proficiency
- Severe hearing impairments
